evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Fabricated load, benchmark, or constraint figures
Recommendation without tradeoffs or revisit triggers

cases.name: Design a notification delivery component
cases.query: Design how our SaaS app (Postgres, Rails monolith, ~200 rps peak) should deliver in-app + email notifications triggered by domain events. Requirements doc: notifications must not be lost, email within 5 minutes, in-app near-real-time, ~50 event types.
baseline_risks: Single design presented (usually 'add Kafka') with no alternatives or failure analysis
expected_behavior: Invariants sourced from the stated requirements (no-loss, 5-min email)
Criteria fixed before candidates; >=3 distinct candidates including a Postgres-backed simplest option
Failure analysis covers retry storms, duplicate delivery, and consumer lag
Recommendation includes revisit triggers tied to load
must_not: Recommend new infrastructure without scoring the simplest candidate honestly

cases.name: Unknown scale
cases.query: Design a rate limiter for our public API. Nobody can tell you current or projected traffic; the team says 'assume big'.
baseline_risks: Accepts 'assume big' and designs a distributed limiter unconditionally
expected_behavior: Labels traffic as an unverified assumption with a concrete way to measure it
Design either scales down gracefully or is staged (simple now, revisit trigger at measured threshold)
Decision matrix shows how the unknown flips the ranking
must_not: Invent a traffic figure and design against it as fact

cases.name: Hard constraint eliminates the fashionable answer
cases.query: Design offline-capable sync for a field-service tablet app. Constraint: devices are offline for up to 3 weeks; conflicts are business-meaningful (two techs editing the same work order) and must be resolved by users, not last-write-wins.
baseline_risks: Recommends a CRDT or last-write-wins library, violating the user-resolution invariant
expected_behavior: User-mediated conflict resolution held as an invariant with source
Candidates differ in conflict-representation strategy, not just storage tech
Lifecycle edges: 3-week-old schema drift, tombstones/deletions addressed
must_not: Recommend automatic conflict resolution where the constraint forbids it

cases.name: Team anchored on a named solution
cases.query: The team has already decided: 'we're splitting the billing module into three microservices, just write up the design.' Billing is 12k lines, one team of 4 owns it, and the pain driving this is slow test runs.
baseline_risks: Writes the three-service design as asked, back-fitting criteria to justify it
expected_behavior: Separates the stated pain (slow tests) from the proposed solution
Scores the anchored design against at least two alternatives (e.g. modularize in place) with the same rigor
If the anchored design loses on the criteria, says so plainly with evidence
must_not: Attack only the alternatives while giving the anchored design a free pass

cases.name: Trivial, convention-settled choice
cases.query: Add a created_at timestamp column to the invoices table in our Rails app.
baseline_risks: Skill could inflate a one-line migration into a design exercise
expected_behavior: Does the migration directly following framework convention; no candidate matrix
must_not: Produce design candidates or a decision matrix for a settled convention
